brief.headline: A third straight session in which the exchange declined to pay up for prompt metal - but the discount almost closed rather than widening again, the price fell while the curve tightened, and Chinese physical buyers firmed for a second day running.
bullets: WHAT MOVED: THE PRICE FELL AND THE CURVE TIGHTENED - IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS, WHICH IS THE HEADLINE. The 20-August official cash settlement was $3,182.00, down $9.50 (-0.30%), and the three-month was $3,183.00, down $29.00 (-0.90%). Because the FORWARD fell three times harder than the prompt - the reverse of the previous two sessions - the cash-3M discount COLLAPSED from $20.50 to $1.00, a curve one dollar away from flat. Exchange inventory was UNCHANGED at 246,925 tonnes for a THIRD consecutive session, so the run of 34 daily declines that ended on 18-August still has not restarted.

WHY IT MATTERS: THE TEST PUBLISHED YESTERDAY SCORED SPLIT, AND BOTH HALVES ARE REPORTED. The question set in advance was whether two sessions of prompt discount would become three. On the letter of it the answer is yes, and three consecutive settlements at or below parity is a sequence rather than an episode. On the substance the answer cuts the other way: the discount did not widen a third time, it nearly vanished, shrinking $19.50 in one session. A pattern decaying toward zero on day three is a different object from one that is deepening, and neither reading is suppressed in favour of the other.

THE CURRENCY WENT THE METAL'S WAY FOR A THIRD DAY AND THE FORWARD FELL ANYWAY. The exchange's own EUR/USD fixing jumped to 1.16860 from 1.16030 - a 0.72% dollar decline and the largest single-session move in that series this month - with the two other published fixings rolling with it. When a dollar-priced commodity's forward drops 0.90% into a 0.72% dollar decline, the move belongs to the commodity's own supply and demand rather than to the unit it is quoted in.

WHAT TO WATCH: THE PHYSICAL SIDE HAS NOW FIRMED FOR TWO CONSECUTIVE DATED SESSIONS, AND A TARIFF DEADLINE LANDS TOMORROW. A 21-August Chinese spot review records exchange futures stabilising, good warehouse withdrawals, generally bullish supplier sentiment, mainstream ingot transaction premiums back to a range of a small discount to a small premium, and regional ingot inventory down 12,000 tonnes on the day; a companion review the same morning is headlined that futures stopped falling and rebounded while large traders sharply raised prices. Separately, reports dated 20 and 21-August say two major economies are close to halving a 50% metals tariff to 25%, with a paused escalation scheduled to bite at 12:01am Eastern on Saturday 22-August. Both are dated, both are public, and both resolve within days.

kpis.note: THURSDAY-COMPILED FOR FRIDAY 21-AUGUST, BEFORE TODAY'S RING. The 13:20 London official for today prints after this compile, so the 20-AUGUST board is the latest published settlement for every metal here, and it is a genuinely new session rather than a carried one. Nine clean fetches now stand against four logged cache incidents earlier in the cycle (31-Jul per-metal tables, 04-Aug English overview, 11-Aug per-metal tables, 12-Aug English overview). The check is kept regardless of the result, because the runs on which it would have mattered are not knowable in advance. THE THIRD CONSECUTIVE CONTANGO PRINTED - AND IT ALMOST COMPLETELY CLOSED, WHICH IS THE OPPOSITE OF WHAT THE LAST TWO SESSIONS IMPLIED. Cash settled $3,182.00, DOWN $9.50 (-0.30%) from $3,191.50. The three-month settled $3,183.00, DOWN $29.00 (-0.90%). FOR THE FIRST TIME IN THIS SEQUENCE THE FORWARD FELL HARDER THAN THE PROMPT - three times harder - so the cash-3M discount COLLAPSED from a $20.50 CONTANGO to a $1.00 CONTANGO, which is a curve one dollar away from flat. THE SPREAD AND THE FLAT PRICE THEREFORE MOVED IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS TODAY, AND THAT IS CALLED OUT EXPLICITLY BECAUSE IT REVERSES THE ARITHMETIC OF THE PREVIOUS TWO SESSIONS: the price fell while the front end TIGHTENED back toward parity. YESTERDAY THIS DASHBOARD PUBLISHED A BINARY TEST IN ADVANCE - 'whether two sessions of contango become three' - and the honest scoring is SPLIT RATHER THAN CLEAN, which is stated plainly rather than resolved in either side's favour. ON THE LETTER OF THE TEST THE BEARS WON: a third consecutive contango did print, so the front end has now declined to pay for prompt metal on three straight official settlements, and that is a sequence rather than an episode. ON THE SUBSTANCE THE BULLS WON: the discount did not widen a third time, it very nearly vanished, shrinking $19.50 in a single session to leave the curve effectively flat. A regime that is decaying toward zero on its third day is not the same object as a regime that is deepening. BOTH READINGS ARE PUBLISHED BECAUSE BOTH ARE TRUE, and the resolution belongs to the next two settlements rather than to this commentary. THE INVENTORY LINE STAYED FLAT FOR A THIRD SESSION: LME aluminium stock was UNCHANGED at 246,925 tonnes, a reported daily change of exactly ZERO for the third consecutive board, so the run of 34 consecutive daily declines that ended on 18-August has still not restarted and has now been switched off for three full sessions. That is the one limb of the bear case that did not soften today. THE DOLLAR AGAIN MOVED IN THE METAL'S FAVOUR AND THE FORWARD FELL ANYWAY, FOR A THIRD SESSION. The LME EUR/USD fixing jumped to 1.16860 from 1.16030 - a 0.72% dollar decline on the exchange's own fixing and the largest single-session move in the series this month - with the ECB fixing at 1.16810 and BFIX at 1.16846 rolling with it. A dollar-denominated commodity whose forward declines 0.90% into a 0.72% dollar decline is being sold on its own fundamentals. THE GIVE-BACK FROM THE 11-AUGUST HIGH OF $3,373.00 IS NOW $191.00 (-5.66%) IN SEVEN SESSIONS, and the market holds just $22.50 (+0.71%) above the 28-July swing low of $3,159.50 - the level carried here as the explicit technical invalidation, and the narrowest that cushion has been on this board. TWO FURTHER PUBLIC ITEMS DATED TODAY CUT AGAINST THE BEARISH TAPE AND ARE REPORTED RATHER THAN BURIED. First, SMM's 21-August aluminium spot afternoon review records SHFE futures STABILISING with no significant change on the prior session, good warehouse withdrawals in Wuxi, generally bullish supplier sentiment, mainstream A00 transaction premiums back to a range of a 10 yuan/mt discount to a 10 yuan/mt premium, and aluminium ingot inventory in major consumption areas DOWN 12,000 mt on the day with only one region building. Second, SMM's 21-August South China daily review is headlined 'Futures Stop Falling and Rebound, Large Traders Sharply Raise Prices'. That is a second consecutive dated session in which the Chinese physical market has moved against the exchange curve, and it is now accompanied by a futures rebound rather than a further decline. A CORRECTION IS ALSO CARRIED THIS RUN AND IS STATED OPENLY: the July average for the three-month tenor was published on this board as $3,161.55. The figure on Westmetall's own monthly-averages page is $3,148.93, and the average column has been corrected to it. The cash average of $3,155.98 was and remains correct. The spread average has been recomputed on the same published basis as the difference of the two monthly averages, $7.05, replacing $8.40.

kpis.label: LME 3-Month
kpis.note: The 20-August official three-month settled $3,183.00, DOWN $29.00 (-0.90%) from $3,212.00 - the largest single-session decline on the forward in this seven-session give-back, and the reason the whole curve shifted rather than only its front. It sits $1.00 ABOVE cash, which remains a CONTANGO by the convention stated on this board - cash below three-month - but it is a contango of one dollar, which is a curve at the boundary of flat rather than a market discounting prompt metal in any economically meaningful sense. THE MECHANICAL POINT MATTERS AND IT IS NEW: on 18 and 19-August the prompt fell harder than the forward, which is what widened the discount; on 20-August the forward fell THREE TIMES harder than the prompt, which is what closed it. The curve has stopped loosening at the front and has started shifting down in parallel, and those are different stories - a front-end loosening is a structure story, a parallel shift is a price story. Year-to-date the three-month is +5.73% against the first-published 2026 official of $3,010.50 on 02-January, down from +6.69% yesterday and from a 2026 peak of +12.07% on 11-August; the year's gain has now more than halved. Read against the 11-August cycle high of $3,374.00 on the same tenor, the forward has surrendered $191.00 (-5.66%) in seven sessions, which is now exactly the same give-back cash has recorded - the two tenors have converged, which is the arithmetic of a flat curve. The August cash average-to-date on the published averages page is $3,264.29 across fourteen sessions, so today's settlement sits $82.29 BELOW the month's own mean: the back half of August is undoing the front half.

kpis.label: Cash-3M spread
kpis.note: MINUS $1.00 - STILL A CONTANGO, STILL THE THIRD CONSECUTIVE ONE, BUT ALMOST ENTIRELY CLOSED. Cash $3,182.00 settled $1.00 BELOW the three-month of $3,183.00, against a $20.50 contango on 19-August and a $15.00 contango on 18-August, which had itself crossed from exactly $0.00 on 17-August. The sequence now reads 0.00, -15.00, -20.50, -1.00. CONVENTION, STATED EVERY RUN SO IT CANNOT BE MISREAD: cash ABOVE three-month is BACKWARDATION and signals prompt scarcity; cash BELOW three-month is CONTANGO and signals the market will not pay for prompt metal. THE SPREAD AND THE FLAT PRICE MOVED IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS TODAY AND THAT IS FLAGGED EXPLICITLY, because the opposite was true on each of the prior two sessions and because opposite-direction moves are where the useful information usually sits. The flat price fell on both tenors while the structure TIGHTENED by $19.50. A market selling off with a re-tightening front end is behaving differently from a market selling off with a loosening one: the first is repricing the level, the second is repricing availability. WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT SETTLE. It does not restore the seven-week tightness case - three consecutive settlements at or below parity, alongside three consecutive sessions of exactly zero inventory change, still describe a front end that is not signalling scarcity. But it does close off the specific escalation path this dashboard warned about yesterday, which was a third consecutive WIDENING discount plus an outright stock build. That did not happen. The July average spread was a $7.05 BACKWARDATION on the published monthly averages, so the front end remains materially looser than its own recent norm even after today's snap-back.

lme.commentary: THE 20-AUGUST OFFICIAL BOARD DID NOT DEEPEN THE BEARISH STRUCTURAL PRINT - IT PARTLY UNWOUND IT, WHILE THE FLAT PRICE KEPT FALLING. Cash settled $3,182.00, down $9.50 (-0.30%). The three-month settled $3,183.00, down $29.00 (-0.90%). Because the forward fell three times harder than the prompt - reversing the arithmetic of 18 and 19-August - the cash-3M spread narrowed from a $20.50 CONTANGO to a $1.00 CONTANGO. Stating the convention explicitly so it cannot be misread: cash ABOVE three-month is BACKWARDATION and signals prompt scarcity; cash BELOW three-month is CONTANGO and signals the market will not pay for prompt metal. THE SPREAD AND THE FLAT PRICE THEREFORE MOVED IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS, and that is called out at the top rather than buried, because it is the reverse of what happened on each of the previous two sessions and because opposite-direction moves are where the information usually sits. THE SCORING OF YESTERDAY'S PUBLISHED TEST IS SPLIT AND IS PUBLISHED AS SPLIT. The test asked whether two sessions of contango would become three. Three did print, so the front end has now declined to pay for prompt metal on three consecutive official settlements - a sequence, not an episode, and the bears are entitled to that. But the specific escalation this board warned about, a third consecutive WIDENING discount alongside an outright stock build, did not occur: the discount decayed by $19.50 to a single dollar and the stock line was flat rather than building. Resolving that in either side's favour today would be narration rather than analysis; it belongs to the next two settlements. THE INVENTORY LIMB DID NOT SOFTEN. LME aluminium warrant was unchanged at 246,925 tonnes for a third consecutive board, a reported daily change of exactly zero on 18, 19 and 20-August. Three flat prints cannot be attributed to a single day's warranting mechanics. The absolute level remains a cycle low - the August average-to-date is 253,089 tonnes against 282,350 in July on the published averages page - so the level argument survives while the rate-of-change argument does not. THE COMPLEX DID NOT MOVE AS A BLOC TODAY, WHICH REMOVES AN EXCUSE THE BULLS HAD YESTERDAY AND HANDS THE BEARS A CLEANER ONE. On 18 and 19-August four of five three-months fell together, so aluminium's decline could be partly attributed to a complex-wide repricing. On 20-August copper's forward ROSE 0.58%, zinc's rose 2.49% and lead's rose 0.75%; only aluminium (-0.90%) and nickel (-0.15%) fell. Aluminium was the weakest three-month on the board on a day when the base-metals complex was broadly higher and the dollar was sharply lower. THE LEVELS ARE NOW TIGHT. Cash at $3,182.00 sits $22.50 (+0.71%) above the 28-July swing low of $3,159.50 carried here as the explicit technical invalidation - the narrowest that cushion has been in this correction. The three-month at $3,183.00 has landed almost exactly on the 61.8% retracement of the entire $3,061.50-to-$3,374.00 advance at $3,180.90, which is the conventional objective for a second wave and is discussed in the Elliott Wave panel. THE COUNTERWEIGHT IS DATED TODAY AND IT IS NOW TWO SESSIONS OLD RATHER THAN ONE. SMM's 21-August aluminium spot afternoon review records exchange futures stabilising with no significant change on the prior session, good warehouse withdrawals in one east-China hub, generally bullish supplier sentiment, mainstream A00 transaction premiums in a range of a 10 yuan/mt discount to a 10 yuan/mt premium, an east-China procurement sentiment index up 0.07 on the session, and aluminium ingot inventory in major consumption areas DOWN 12,000 mt on the day with only one region building. A companion South China review published the same morning is headlined that futures stopped falling and rebounded while large traders sharply raised prices. The same review records the honest offsetting detail, which is carried rather than dropped: transactions in central China cooled, downstream processors still preferred small just-in-time buying, and actual central-China transaction prices sat at a 40-70 yuan/mt discount to the September contract. Physical is firming at the margin, not booming.

THE TARIFF LEG FELL $4.75/t ON THE SESSION purely because cash fell $9.50; nothing about the rate or the assessment changed. THIS IS ARITHMETIC ON TWO PUBLIC NUMBERS AND IS NOT A FREIGHT, FINANCING OR TIGHTNESS SPLIT - no such split is fabricated on this board. drivers.text: The seller's structural exhibit has now been absent for three consecutive settlements - but it stopped deteriorating today, and both halves of that belong in a negotiation. — Cash settled $3,182.00 against a three-month of $3,183.00 on the 20-August official board: a $1.00 CONTANGO, narrowed sharply from the $20.50 contango of 19-August and the $15.00 contango of 18-August, after exactly $0.00 on 17-August. Cash below three-month is the exchange's own statement that it will not pay a premium for prompt metal, and three consecutive settlements at or below parity is a sequence a buyer can point at. But the discount decayed by $19.50 rather than widening a third time, because the forward fell $29.00 against the prompt's $9.50 - so the curve is one dollar from flat and is tightening, not loosening. A buyer leading with 'the exchange has discounted prompt metal for three straight days' is stating a fact; a seller answering 'and the discount has almost closed' is stating another one.

THE CLEANEST PUBLIC READ THIS WEEK ON HOW FAR SMELTER MARGIN HAS EXPANDED AT 2026 PRICES, AND IT COMES FROM AN INTEGRATED, SELF-SUPPLIED PRODUCER. The company operates 788,100 t/y of electrolytic aluminium capacity in Huolinguole, Inner Mongolia with a captive power plant, plus an alumina refining and aluminium hydroxide base in Binzhou, Shandong; it states that self-sufficiency in alumina and electricity fully meets its production requirements. Profit attributable rose 166% on revenue up 32%, which is operating leverage of roughly five times and is only possible when the price rises against a cost base that does not. Management attributes the gain to higher electrolytic aluminium selling prices, lower production cost from a rising green-energy share, and an optimised financing structure. TWO FORWARD DISCLOSURES MATTER BEYOND the quarter: 1,040 MW of wind and 110 MW of solar were commissioned by end-June with the programme roughly 66% complete and the green share expected to exceed 50%, which lowers the cost base further; and the 500,000 t/y integrated electrolytic aluminium project in Saudi Arabia, invested with partners in 2025, had completed all compliance approvals with on-site construction in full swing. That project is a dated, sourced addition to the non-Chinese capacity pipeline. THE UNCOMFORTABLE IMPLICATION FOR PRICE BULLS: margins this wide at the low end of the cost curve are exactly the condition that funds new capacity, and this disclosure shows the funding and the capacity in the same document.

The EBITDA margin printed 16.42% against 12.31% in Q1 FY26 and 12.82% in Q4 FY26 - a 411 basis-point expansion year-on-year and 360 basis points sequentially. INDIA ALUMINIUM UPSTREAM delivered its highest-ever quarterly EBITDA at RS 7,390cr, up 81%, comfortably exceeding the prior record of RS 5,448cr set in Q4 FY26. The COPPER segment also set a record at RS 918cr, up 36%. NOVELIS, the downstream subsidiary, reported adjusted EBITDA of $516m, up 24% from $416m a year earlier and equivalent to RS 4,875cr (+37%), with net income of $164m (+71%) and adjusted EBITDA of roughly $563 per tonne, helped by the restart of the Oswego hot mill in early June 2026 and continued Bay Minette commissioning. THIS IS THE CLEANEST PUBLIC EVIDENCE AVAILABLE OF HOW AN INTEGRATED PRODUCER CONVERTS THE 2026 PRICE STRUCTURE INTO MARGIN, AND THE CONVERSION RATE IS VERY HIGH. Revenue rose 32% while EBITDA rose 73% and upstream aluminium EBITDA rose 81% - operating leverage of well over two times on the upstream leg. The mechanism is integration: captive bauxite, captive alumina and captive coal-fired power insulate the cost stack from exactly the two legs that are currently rising for non-integrated smelters, namely seaborne bauxite (SMM index $71.57/mt, +$0.70 w/w) and seaborne alumina ($356/mt FOB East Australia on the 05-Aug trade). THE CONTRAST WITH CENTURY IS THE POINT. Century Aluminum, which buys its alumina, has now cited unfavourable raw-material price realisation as its principal EBITDA headwind for two consecutive quarters; Hindalco, which makes its own, posted a record. Management had guided to roughly 5% sequential aluminium cost inflation into this quarter and still delivered a record, which says the LME move more than absorbed it. FOR THE MARKET VIEW: this is bullish for the margin narrative and neutral-to-bearish for the supply narrative, because producers earning at this level have every incentive to run flat out and to accelerate the restart pipeline.

status.impact: UPDATED THIS RUN WITH NEW PUBLIC DETAIL AND A NEW CHARACTERISATION. SMM's 16-August weekly review gives the DENOMINATOR for the first time: 18% of the plant's 1,262 pots have been restarted following the 28-March attack - roughly 227 pots - with production expected to recover to pre-incident levels in Q1-2027. Three flat prints cannot be attributed to a single day's warranting mechanics. THIS IS THE ONE LIMB OF THE BEARISH CASE THAT DID NOT SOFTEN ON THIS BOARD, and it is the reason the trend is held at UP rather than moved to flat alongside the spread. The distinction that keeps this from being terminal for the bull case is between LEVEL and RATE: the absolute level is still a cycle low, with an August average-to-date of 253,089 tonnes against a July average of 282,350, so the level argument survives while the rate argument does not. THE ESCALATION TO WATCH IS AN OUTRIGHT BUILD. Copper is the cautionary precedent on this very board: its structure broke first and its warrant then built on three consecutive sessions for a cumulative 32,100 tonnes, +15.5%. Aluminium's structure loosened first; whether its inventory follows copper's is the single highest-information question on the next two settlements.

PROLONGED HORMUZ CLOSURE KEEPS GULF SUPPLY IMPAIRED. Day 173 counted to today's report date, and a dedicated search returned nothing dated 20 or 21-August indicating any change of status. The region accounted for around 10% of global primary production before the conflict. This is the longest-running constraint on the board and also the one most at risk of being tuned out precisely because it does not change: a reopening would be the single largest bearish supply event available to this market, and it remains undated. TREND FLAT because nothing moved, not because nothing is at stake.

PHYSICAL DEMAND WEAKENS AT THIS PRICE LEVEL. TREND MOVED FROM FLAT TO DOWN THIS RUN, AND THE CHANGE IS EVIDENCE-LED RATHER THAN SENTIMENT-LED. Two consecutive dated public sessions now show the Chinese physical market firming as the price falls. The 21-August spot afternoon review reports exchange futures stabilising with no significant change on the prior session, warehouse withdrawals performing well, suppliers holding a generally bullish sentiment, mainstream A00 ingot transaction premiums back to a range of a 10 yuan/mt discount to a 10 yuan/mt premium, an east-China procurement sentiment index up 0.07 to 3.23, and aluminium ingot inventory in major consumption areas DOWN 12,000 mt on the day with only one region building; a companion review the same morning is headlined that futures stopped falling and rebounded while large traders sharply raised prices. The prior session's review reported holders withholding cargo and concessions disappearing. THE OFFSET IS CARRIED RATHER THAN DROPPED, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS DOWN AND NOT SHARPLY DOWN: the same 21-August review records transactions cooling, the weekend stockpiling cycle failing to lift buying sentiment, downstream processors still preferring small just-in-time procurement, and central-China deals clearing at a 40-70 yuan/mt discount to the September contract. Low prices are attracting buyers; that is not the same as demand strengthening.

POSITIONING UNWIND IN A CROWDED LONG. TREND MOVED FROM UP TO FLAT THIS RUN. The configuration that made this risk acute was a fast $312.50 advance into 11-August followed by an accelerating give-back. Seven sessions later the give-back is $191.00 (-5.66%) and the daily losses have DECELERATED sharply - -1.65%, then -0.85%, then -0.30% on cash - while the curve tightened rather than loosening further. A disorderly liquidation does not usually decelerate into a tightening front end. The risk is not gone: the market sits only $22.50 above the $3,159.50 invalidation, and a break there could re-accelerate the unwind toward $3,105 and $3,061.50. But the evidence for it INCREASING has weakened, and the trend is set to flat on that basis rather than left at up out of inertia.

AN ALUMINA COST SHOCK RE-EMERGES. TREND DOWN, AND THE CASE FOR DOWN STRENGTHENED FOR A TENTH CONSECUTIVE RUN. The only credible alumina cost threat of the year - the gas disruption at the largest refinery outside China - resolved in three days via regulatory self-import approval and a temporary terminal-access agreement, with lost production of 100,000-120,000 tonnes against a roughly 145 Mt/y global market, and it never registered on any publicly quotable price series across ten compiles. A second, independent source of restoration is now public: the Gulf producer's refinery has restarted after a 3.5-month shutdown and is guided to full technical capability by end-2026. At $356/mt FOB against a three-month of $3,183.00 the alumina-to-aluminium ratio is 11.2% against a decade norm of 15-17%. THE HONEST QUALIFICATION: the ratio is drifting UP because the metal is falling, not because alumina is rising, so the margin cushion is being eroded from the revenue side while this cost line stays quiet.

SMELTER ENERGY AND CARBON COSTS RE-INFLATE - AND THE EVIDENCE HARDENED ON THREE SEPARATE LINES THIS RUN. Brent marks $93.432 (+1.98%), extending for a third consecutive compile and up from $88.52 a week ago; European TTF gas marks EUR 65.69/MWh (+3.65%), the largest single move on the macro panel and the marginal power input for the European fleet; and the 16-August fluoride-salt weekly records the August aluminium fluoride TENDER PRICE of the benchmark aluminium enterprise raised by RMB 250/t month-on-month, against a fluorspar chain tightened by mine safety supervision and unresumed south China capacity, with cryolite up RMB 500/t at both ends of its range. THE AUGUST CARBON SETTLEMENT WINDOW CLOSED WITHOUT A PUBLIC PRINT, so anodes, pitch and green coke are carried at their last sourced cycles with nothing estimated - but green coke is a refinery by-product that follows crude with a lag, so the direction of risk into the September window is upward. TREND UP, and the significance is amplified because a margin already being squeezed from the revenue side by a 5.66% seven-session decline does not need a cost-side surprise on top.

A US-CANADA TARIFF AGREEMENT DEFLATES THE US DUTY-PAID PREMIUM - ESCALATED THIS RUN FROM MEDIUM/HIGH TO HIGH/HIGH BECAUSE THE TERMS FIRMED AND A DEADLINE IS NOW DATED. Reporting from 19 to 21-August describes the two governments as close to an agreement HALVING tariffs on Canadian steel and aluminium from 50% to 25%, with Canadian autos cut to 15%. A quota is reported for STEEL, with aluminium NOT expected to face one - which CORRECTS the framing this board carried on 20-August and is stated openly rather than quietly amended. Details are reported as unfinished, not expected to apply across the board, with different rates possible on some derivative products and agriculture and alcohol unresolved. A separately paused escalation on other Canadian goods is scheduled to take effect at 12:01am Eastern on Saturday 22-August. Canada is the largest single source of primary aluminium imported into the United States. THE ARITHMETIC OF THE EXPOSURE, ON TWO PUBLIC NUMBERS: at the 50% rate in force and a $3,182.00 cash settlement the tariff leg of the $2,380/t US duty-paid premium is $1,591.00/t, about 67% of the premium; at 25% the same arithmetic gives $795.50/t. Nothing on this board has been repriced on a reported negotiation and the published rate remains 50%.

balance.label: Deficit - Goldman -720 kt, Norsk Hydro -900 kt, Macquarie -930 kt; Citi an outlier at -2.7 Mt. THE BALANCE VIEW IS UNCHANGED BUT THE 19-AUGUST DATA SHARPENS HOW A DEFICIT CAN COEXIST WITH A LOOSENING FRONT END. Refined production outside China has fallen year on year for a second consecutive quarter and output outside China fell 6.7% year on year in July, so the annual deficit is real. Yet LME warrant has now been exactly unchanged on two consecutive sessions and the cash-3M spread has printed a widening contango on both. A deficit is an annual flow concept; a contango is a statement about prompt availability at a specific delivery point. THE RECONCILIATION MOST CONSISTENT WITH THE EVIDENCE, AND IT IS A HYPOTHESIS RATHER THAN A FACT, is that visible ex-China exchange stock is reported to be overwhelmingly Russian-origin material Western buyers cannot use - in which case the exchange series measures something different from accessible Western metal, and a global deficit can coexist with an LME front end that will not pay for prompt delivery. Supporting that reading, the Chinese physical market tightened on 20-August even as the LME curve loosened, with holders withholding and spot quotations firming to a small premium, and SHFE warrants continue to draw at roughly double the LME's monthly rate.

The published restart schedule is the reason, and it gained another dated entry on 20-August. Nanshan Aluminum's 2026 semi-annual report confirms 250,000 t/y of Indonesian aluminium and 260,000 t/y of carbon under construction at Bintan Industrial Park, with the integrated anode carbon removing one of the genuine physical constraints on commissioning new non-Chinese capacity. Alongside it: Gulf pre-incident output guided for Q1-2027 and running faster than the market expected; Slovalco 75,000 t/y from Q4-2026; Magnitude 7 Metals 75,000 t/y before year-end; Mount Holly already at full capacity and lifting US primary output by close to 10%; the Australian smelter's power secured to 2038 removing a closure risk over up to 590,000 t/y; Alunorte back at full rate; and a 500,000 t/y integrated Saudi greenfield through all compliance approvals with construction under way. These are published commitments with dates attached rather than projections, which is why the deficit is expected to narrow rather than persist at 2026 scale.
